intro: Professionals and everyday users convert fluid ounces (us) (fl oz) to cups (us) (cup) when working across us_customary and us_customary standards in culinary recipe scaling, beverage bottling, laboratory reagent preparation, and fluid tank capacity sizing. One fluid ounce (us) equals 0.125 cups (us), while 1 cup (us customary) equals 8 fluid ounces (us). Whether you are verifying volume & liquid specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: US Customary vs. British Imperial Liquid Volume Trap
items: US Customary and UK Imperial liquid units share identical names but have different physical volumes: 1 US Gallon is 3.78541 L (128 US fl oz), whereas 1 UK Imperial Gallon is 4.54609 L (160 Imp fl oz) — a 20.1% difference.

Similarly, 1 US Pint contains 16 US fluid ounces (473.18 mL), while 1 British Imperial Pint contains 20 Imperial fluid ounces (568.26 mL). Always verify whether your recipe, pump datasheet, or vehicle spec sheet uses US or UK standards.

faqs.question: How many cups (us) (cup) are in 1 fluid ounce (us) (fl oz)?
faqs.answer: There are 0.125 cups (us) (cup) in 1 fluid ounce (us) (fl oz), which rounds to 0.125 cup for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 cup (us customary) equals 8 fluid ounces (us).

faqs.question: How do I convert fluid ounces (us) to cups (us) (fl oz to cup)?
faqs.answer: To convert fluid ounces (us) to cups (us), use the formula: cup = fl oz × 0.125. For example, converting 8 fl oz gives 1 cup.

faqs.question: What is 8 fluid ounces (us) in cups (us)?
faqs.answer: 8 fluid ounces (us) (fl oz) equals exactly 1 cups (us) (cup) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
